h2: Pool Repair Ubud – Leaks, Tiles, Grout & Pipework
intro: A pool quietly losing water, shedding mosaic tiles, or clogging its skimmer every two days is a familiar sight across Ubud's hillside villas. Pool Repair Ubud jobs often trace back to the same local factors: constant humidity, spring or well-water chemistry, and relentless jungle debris. I'll walk you through what needs fixing first so you're not paying for everything at once.

sections.h3: Why Ubud's Climate Wears Pools Down Faster
sections.text: Villas in Sayan and the surrounding river valleys sit in thick, damp air year-round. That moisture seeps into grout lines, corrodes stainless fittings, and keeps mould alive behind tile edges. On sloped plots, pump pressure fluctuates as water climbs from lower tanks, which stresses joints and weakens old pipework. The result is a pool that seems fine one month and starts weeping at the coping stones the next.

sections.h3: What I Typically Find on Site
sections.text: Most calls I get from villas around Penestanan fall into four buckets: slow water loss with no visible crack, mosaic tiles popping up after a dry season, grout that's turned white-powdery and crumbling, and pipe joints weeping near the filter housing. Because many of these pools were built fifteen to twenty years ago, the original sealant has simply expired. I assess each issue on site and tell you honestly whether it's a patch job or something structural.

sections.h3: Pool Repair Ubud – What to Send Me First
sections.text: Before I book a visit, send me a short WhatsApp message with three things: a photo or video of the problem area (tiles, grout line, pipe joint, or water level), how long you've noticed it, and whether your villa runs off a well, spring, or PDAM supply. If the pool is losing more than a centimetre a day, mention that too. From those details I can usually give you a rough direction and let you know if an on-site inspection is needed.

The single biggest enemy in Nyuh Kuning and similar jungle settings is leaf fall. Pull the skimmer basket daily, clear the surface with a net before leaves sink and decompose, and flush the filter once a week during wet season. Keep bathroom ventilation running so damp air doesn't migrate toward pool equipment. A quick monthly check of grout lines and tile edges—pressing gently to feel for softness—catches problems while they're still a small repair.

faq.q: How do I know if my pool has a leak or is just evaporating?
faq.a: Mark the water level with tape, wait 24 hours with the pump off, then check again. If it dropped noticeably without rain, there's likely a leak worth investigating.

faq.q: Can you fix loose mosaic tiles without draining the whole pool?
faq.a: In most cases yes—I can re-adhere individual tiles or small patches from above the waterline. For larger areas or structural cracks a partial drain may be needed, which I'll flag before starting.

faq.q: Do well-water villas need different pool maintenance?
faq.a: Yes. Mineral-heavy spring and well water accelerates scale on fittings and clogs filters faster, so UV systems and pre-filters benefit from more frequent servicing in those setups.
